A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research framework, renamed from AdvPrompt to WHISPER. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including the additional material in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original mathematical benchmark evaluations, commercial-API experiments and analyses of prompt perspectives, transfer across models, refinement and development-set reliability.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds GEPA comparisons, another model configuration, science and commonsense evaluations, and an output-safety examination.

M1.justification: The five prompt perspectives, GPT-4o generator, accuracy filtering, response-length ranking and iterative top-k refinement remain unchanged. Renaming AdvPrompt to WHISPER and regrouping the existing perspectives under four category headings do not introduce a new procedure.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates mathematical reasoning on GSM8K, MATH-500, AMC 2023 and AIME 2024. v2 retains these and adds GPQA-Diamond science questions and CommonsenseQA, substantially extending task and domain coverage beyond mathematics.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds GEPA to comparisons on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-LLaMA-8B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B and Qwen3-14B. This introduces a directly relevant automatic prompt optimizer beyond v1's fixed prompting baselines and DEER. The original comparator sets remain in the corresponding appendix experiments.

E3.justification: v2 adds the DeepSeek-R1-Distill-LLaMA-8B configuration and an independent author-review protocol covering 300 sampled outputs. Section 6.2 specifies that the new domain evaluations reuse math-optimized prompts unchanged. Existing mathematical development-set construction, decoding settings and generation budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 6.2 adds an explicit test of transfer from mathematics to science and commonsense reasoning. Appendix B.6 adds harmful-output examination and five illustrated cases in Figures 10–14. Earlier perspective, model-transfer, sensitivity, refinement and development-set analyses are retained, including heatmaps moved between main text and appendix.

E5.justification: Appendix B.6 newly reports inter-annotator agreement for the safety examination, giving 100% agreement. The original three/eight samples-per-question reporting is unchanged, and no confidence intervals or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: v2 adds GEPA, LLaMA-8B, science, commonsense and safety/case results. Figure 3 revises reported token reductions from 35% to 46% for Claude and 47% to 50% for Gemini; Claude's method accuracy changes from 93.4% to 96.4%, while its CoT baseline also changes. The PDFs do not explain these revisions. All 42 original mathematics comparison rows retain their numerical values after matching relocated tables.

T1.justification: The optimization objective, i.i.d. development-set assumption and Equations (1)–(2) remain unchanged. Neither version supplies theorems or proofs; v2's expanded conceptual motivation introduces no new mathematical result.

C1.justification: The central claim of training-free, black-box token reduction while preserving reasoning performance remains. v2 extends the abstract, contribution list and conclusion to claim generalizability across data domains, and updates the headline commercial-API reduction claims from 35%/47% to 46%/50%.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 adds explanations involving empathy, social behavior and the influence of contextual evidence. Section 5.2 interprets the GEPA comparison as supporting perspective diversity and proposes complementarity with white-box approaches; Section 6.2 adds a domain-generalizability interpretation. The principal larger-model and limited-perspective limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 identifies DSPy and the same GPT-4o version as GEPA implementation details. It adds LLaMA-8B prompt indices but removes the previously disclosed Evidence-IV example and its Qwen3-8B index entry. The printed code-access path changes from AdvPrompt to Whisper. Existing hyperparameters, hardware and evaluation-script information remain available.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially redirects positioning from automated adversarial attacks and reasoning disruption toward persuasive, psychological and role-play prompting. References such as AdvPrompter and AutoDAN are removed, while GEPA, DSPy, Kong et al. and additional psychology/in-context-learning works are introduced. This changes the relationship to prior research beyond terminology or bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: Beyond the pervasive AdvPrompt/WHISPER and adversarial/persuasive renaming, the abstract, introduction, related-work discussion and prompt-category motivation undergo substantial rewriting. The contribution narrative is reorganized and expanded, although the overall main-section sequence remains.

P2.justification: v2 adds the out-of-domain Table 2 and five case figures, restructures Table 1 around three models with GEPA rows, and consolidates retained model results into expanded appendix tables. Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-14B heatmaps exchange main-text/appendix placement, and several existing figures are relocated or relabeled.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked an automatic prompt-optimization comparator and evaluation beyond mathematics. GEPA comparisons in Table 1 and transfer of unchanged math-optimized prompts in Table 2 substantially strengthen scrutiny of comparative effectiveness and generalizability. The bounded safety examination adds useful evidence. Unexplained API-score revisions and removal of a disclosed prompt reduce transparency locally, but do not outweigh these substantive empirical gains.
